1.explanation: Both of these Lua filters are responsible for generating the HTML structure and class attributes for panel-based tabsets before Pandoc conversion. panel-tabset.lua parses the block’s attribute list (including .nav-fill) and hands off layout details to panel-layout.lua. panel-layout.lua is where the <ul class="nav nav-tabs ..."> tag is created and its classes assigned. Because the .nav-fill class from the block attributes is no longer being forwarded into the class list on the <ul> in panel-layout.lua, Bootstrap’s fill behavior is lost. Fixing this will require updating these filters so that any .nav-* utility classes from the original block attributes are merged into the <ul class="nav nav-tabs"> element rather than remaining on the outer wrapper alone.
1.bug_scenario:
The user is trying to combine a panel-tabset with Bootstrap’s .nav-fill utility to distribute tabs evenly across the width of the container. In Quarto 1.2.x the following QMD works as expected (tabs fill the full width):

    ::: {.panel-tabset .nav-fill}
    ## A
    ## B
    :::

However in Quarto 1.3.x the .nav-fill class no longer takes effect when placed alongside .panel-tabset on the same container (the tabs collapse to their intrinsic width). Reversing the class order (applying .nav-fill on the outer container and .panel-tabset on the next inner container) restores the fill behavior. This indicates that the logic which reads the panel-tabset attribute list and wires up the Bootstrap nav classes is no longer propagating .nav-fill onto the actual <ul class="nav nav-tabs"> element.

The provided screenshots show:
- In 1.2.x: tabs stretch full width
- In 1.3.x: tabs shrink to fit

2.explanation:
Quarto’s tabset support is implemented via a Pandoc Lua filter in `panel-tabset.lua`, which reads the incoming Div attributes (including `.nav-fill`) and is supposed to forward `nav-fill` onto the inner `<nav class="nav">`. In the 1.3.x prerelease that promotion no longer happens — the class stays on the outer wrapper, so Bootstrap never sees it on the actual nav. 

The shared logic for panels (including tabsets) lives in `panel-layout.lua`, which provides the helper routines that `panel-tabset.lua` calls to build the nav. Both files would need to be updated so that any `.nav-fill` (or similar nav-related) class in the source Div ends up on the `<nav>` element rather than on the wrapper. Adjusting these two files restores correct Bootstrap behavior without requiring end users to swap class order manually.
2.bug_scenario:
The reporter is trying to combine Quarto’s panel-tabset feature with Bootstrap’s `nav-fill` utility class, by writing

```markdown
:::{.panel-tabset .nav-fill}

## A

## B

:::
```

Under Quarto 1.2.x this correctly emits a tabbed panel whose tab headers stretch evenly across the full width. In the new 1.3.x prerelease the tabs still appear, but the `.nav-fill` class is no longer applied to the actual `<nav class="nav">` element that Bootstrap styles, so you get only the plain panel style rather than a full-width fill. Swapping the class order (i.e. nesting `.nav-fill` outside `.panel-tabset`) awkwardly restores the right behavior, which confirms that the Lua filter is simply mis-placing the class.

The attached screenshots show:
- Quarto 1.2.x: two full-width tab headers (correct)
- Quarto 1.3.x prerelease: default panel styling, no fill (broken)
